aj: Quick capacity question — marketing says Nov promos + holiday ramp could ~2x our current peak. How many reserved GPU-hours should we commit for Q4 to keep p95 latency <200ms and 99% availability? Need rough calc by EOD.

maria: Do we have an updated workload mix? last Q3 numbers were 68% small-chat (<1k tokens), 22% long-form (1k-8k), 10% embeddings/rerank.

aj: Yep same mix, but expected average request length up ~25% during promos. Current global peak = ~1.3M tokens/s, ~7.5k concurrent sessions.

maria: quick back-of-envelope: our serving runstate: ~12k tokens/s per A100-equivalent GPU for mixed small+long (with batching & kv cache). So at 1.3M tokens/s that's ~108 GPUs at peak. If traffic doubles, ~216 GPUs. Add 20% headroom -> ~260 GPUs.

sasha: That 12k/s/GPU assumes continuous batching and ~150 token responses. If avg tokens/request jumps 25% we lose batching efficiency. I'd model conservative 9.5k tokens/s/GPU for promo window.

derek: Cost side — reserved commit vs on-demand: reserved reduces $/GPU-hour ~35% but requires steady utilization. If we reserve 260 GPUs for a month: GPU-hours = 260 * 24 * 30 = 187200 GPU-hours. At reserved rate $1.50/hr -> $280.8k. On-demand at $2.30/hr would be $430.56k. But if utilization <70% we might waste money.

aj: We need target utilization during promo. Ops wants 99% SLO, marketing wants no throttles. Let's simulate a ramp profile for Nov 15-30 (peak windows 6h/day). Can someone run a short sim with these params?

maria: I'll queue a ramp-sim job. Params I'll use: concurrency_peak=15k, token_peak=2.6M/s, model_mix=[small:0.68,long:0.22,embed:0.10], avg_tokens=+25%, batching_eff=0.8. Command: `./tools/ramp-sim --concurrency 15000 --tokens 2600000 --mix small:0.68,long:0.22,embed:0.1 --avg-inflation 1.25 --batch-eff 0.8`

ops-bot: Run started by maria at 2026-02-12T15:28:10Z — job id sim-20260212-4271. Estimated runtime 4m.

maria: Early sim output (first minute): required GPUs @ conservative 9.5k/s ~= 274 GPUs peak. 20% safety margin -> 329 GPUs. Estimated monthly GPU-hours for a 2-week promo tail (peak windows only) ~ 20k reserved-equivalent hours.

derek: If those numbers hold, reserved commit for just the promo window via short-term reserved (1mo) plus autoscale for rest makes sense. Proposal: commit 350 GPUs for Nov month, enable burst on-demand for +30% headroom. That hedges availability and keeps cost roughly at reserved rate for the committed slice.

sasha: Also check regional constraints — APAC region has lower spare capacity for our instance family. If we shift some weight to us-east/us-west we need cross-region latency fallback and costs for egress. We should identify top-5 customers by latency sensitivity and pin them to regions.

aj: Good point. Also include networking capacity — NAT/gateway limits showed near-saturation last Black Friday test at ~9k concurrent egress connections per AZ. We may need to pre-provision extra NAT instances.

maria: I'll export a follow-up with full sim CSV + per-region GPU need by EOD. Will include util vs cost curves and a recommended reserve commit (3 options: conservative 250 GPUs, mid 300 GPUs, aggressive 350 GPUs).

derek: Nice. For the finance folks, include expected cost delta vs current spend and break-even utilization for each commit option.

aj: Thanks — tag me when you post results. :thumbsup:
